title: I built an autonomous civilization engine where the AI plays the game for you. You just drop a few LLM agents onto the grid and watch. They figure out how to farm, reproduce, build temples, and die of old age, inventing their own history entirely from scratch while you just sit back and observe.
author: Patient-Towel-4840
selftext:
So this is a zero-player civilization game. I wanted to see what happens when wire the agents to run a civilization.

It’s essentially a zero-player civilization game. You don’t give commands. Every few ticks, the engine packages an agent's vitals, memories, and environment, and routes it through OpenRouter. The LLM runs an OODA loop based on Maslow's hierarchy of needs and chooses a physical action.

They have to plant wheat, wait for it to mature, and eat it before their health hits zero. They reproduce, trade, build structures, and eventually die of old age.

They also manage diplomacy through a background trust graph, and usually end up declaring war over a patch of digital stone. If an agent invents a religion, they can convince the farmers to become Priests. The ideology spreads, the crops rot, and the civilization starves.

I don't play as a character. I just sit in a "Demiurge" dashboard where I can read their cognitive logs, or inject a famine or a plague to see how their society handles sudden scarcity.

You can leave the server running for few hundred ticks. The result was that some agents completely abandoned farming to build a barracks, and half the map had died trying to cross deep water to attack their neighbors. They can also cause holy wars between the two civilizations.  
[https://github.com/SpaceCypher/doxa](https://github.com/SpaceCypher/doxa)

comments.author: affabledrunk
comments.body:
Very nice. I also like playing a little god. "Unleash the Plague of Locusts!"

For your control/AI it sounds like you are implementing heuristic type AI or are you actually having an LLM directly play? I'm curious if an LLM can actually play these type of games well. I'm doing a heuristic AI based civ-like also and i sometimes wonder if I couldn't just wire in my codex API key and have Codex play the AI directly although I guess that would rapidly blow my tokens.

replies.author: Patient-Towel-4840
replies.body:
It’s actually the LLM playing directly. There are no underlying heuristics making the decisions every single choice to farm, build, or attack comes from the LLM evaluating its vitals against Maslow's hierarchy and outputting a JSON action.

You're completely right about the token cost, though. If you run 50 agents on every single physics tick, the token cost goes kaboom.  
To solve this, I had to build a social hierarchy. Only "Operation" tier agents (the leaders, priests, etc.) actually ping the API to make independent cognitive decisions. The bulk of the civilization are "Apprentices" who don't make LLM calls; they just shadow the Operation agents and mimic their physical tasks. I also had to strictly cap their episodic memory so the prompt doesn't infinitely expand.

comments.author: shadowlands-mage

amazing!  can you share how the agent "see" the map? the got row data or they vision?  
how the run commands? API  requests or native  or MCP?

replies.author: Patient-Towel-4840
replies.body:
They "see" via raw data injected into their own prompt the backend translates their local grid radius into text descriptions like *"To your north is water, an enemy is 2 tiles east."*

For commands, it's completely native. The LLM simply outputs a structured JSON response like `{"action": "BUILD_TEMPLE"}`, which the Python physics engine parses and executes directly in the game loop no MCP needed!
